proposals.headline: Let host apps read the document as data: outline, paragraphs, tables, any cell range, slide text
proposals.today_caption: Today (embedded Word document): the only read API is getSelection(), which in Word returns the caret only, and in Excel only the user's current selection (max 10,000 cells, values without formulas). To answer "summarize this", a host has to unzip and parse the OOXML itself.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: the host's agent calls el.getContent() and gets the title, a heading outline and typed blocks (paragraphs with style, tables as rows) that match what is on screen; badges show which block each part came from. getRange() reads any sheet range with formulas; PowerPoint returns slide titles, text and notes.
proposals.why: Hosts that put Nitro next to an AI agent need the document's content, not just its pixels: to summarize, answer questions, cite (with #620 highlights) or index it. Nitro has already parsed the whole model in its worker, so returning it as plain JSON is cheap, and it saves every host from shipping a second OOXML parser that can disagree with what the user sees. OnlyOffice and Collabora expose similar document-builder and UNO reads; Office.js has body.getText, tables and range.values.
proposals.effort_note: 3–4 days (getContent() per format from the worker model: docx title/outline/blocks with style, list level and table rows; xlsx getRange(address, {formulas, formats}) for any sheet plus getContent() sheet list with used ranges; pptx slides with title, shape text in reading order and notes; block ids that line up with getSelection/setPosition/highlights; size limits with truncated flags; TypeScript types, React handle methods)
proposals.risk: Low. Read-only and additive: no writes, no undo entries, never marks the file dirty. The main risk is a stable, documented JSON shape; it is versioned (schema: 1) and covered by contract tests so later engine changes don't break hosts.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: the serializer runs in the existing worker and ships in the lazy host-API chunk (a few KB). Reads are on demand, streamed in chunks for huge documents, and never block painting; a test keeps a 1,000-page docx outline under 50 ms.
dod: <nitro-docx>.getContent() returns { schema: 1, format, title, outline[], blocks[] } with paragraphs (text, style, list level), tables (rows of cell text) and images (alt text); outline entries point at block ids.

<nitro-xlsx>.getRange('Sheet!A1:F200', { formulas, formats }) returns values, formulas and number formats for any range on any sheet (not only the selection); getContent() lists sheets with used ranges; large reads are chunked with a truncated flag.
<nitro-pptx>.getContent() returns slides with title, shape text in reading order (shape ids) and speaker notes.
Reads never change selection, focus, scroll position or dirty state; ids line up with getSelection, setPosition and setHighlights (#620); React exposes the same methods on the handle.
TypeScript types and a README section with an agent example; contract tests on python-docx / openpyxl / python-pptx fixtures; bundle-budget and all required checks green.

proposals.headline: Resize, AutoFit and hide rows and columns by dragging header borders, like Excel
proposals.today_caption: Today (dragging the border between column A and B to the right): nothing happens. The cursor never becomes a resize arrow, no width tip appears and the column stays the same, so long labels stay cut off. There is no Format menu for Row Height, Column Width or Hide & Unhide.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: dragging column A's border shows Excel's resize cursor, a dashed guide and a live 'Width: 22.14 (160 pixels)' tip; double-click AutoFits. A Format button in Home › Cells opens Row Height…, Column Width…, AutoFit and Hide & Unhide (Ctrl+9 / Ctrl+0).
proposals.why: Widening a column so a label or number fits is one of the most common things anyone does in a spreadsheet, and today a value like '########' or a cut-off label cannot be fixed at all. Excel, Google Sheets, OnlyOffice and Collabora all resize on a header-border drag and AutoFit on double-click. Nitro's engine already has row height, column width and hide/unhide edits (ported in #67), so this is mostly pointer handling and the Format menu.
proposals.effort_note: 2–3 days (resize hit zone on header borders with cursor, guide and size tip; drag applies to all selected rows/columns; double-click AutoFit using the existing text measurer; Format menu in Cells: Row Height…, AutoFit Row Height, Column Width…, AutoFit Column Width, Default Width…, Hide & Unhide; Ctrl+9 / Ctrl+0 / Ctrl+Shift+9; hidden marker in headers; one undo step each). The right-click entries in #557 call these same commands.
proposals.risk: Low. Writes standard <col width customWidth hidden> and <row ht customHeight hidden>, which the engine already models; untouched columns must round-trip unchanged. Frozen panes and merged cells need to repaint correctly after a resize. Cells gains one large button and stays two rows; Font and Alignment groups are unchanged.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: a few KB in the lazily loaded Excel editor chunk. Dragging shows a guide only and re-lays out the grid once on release, as Excel does; AutoFit measures only the column's used cells (batched, one measure pass).
dod: Hovering a row or column header border shows a resize cursor; dragging shows a guide and a live size tip in Excel units and pixels, and applies on release to every selected row or column, as one undo step.

Double-clicking a border AutoFits to the widest/tallest content (multi-selection too); Home › Cells › Format has Row Height…, AutoFit Row Height, Column Width…, AutoFit Column Width, Default Width… and Hide & Unhide.
Hidden rows and columns are skipped in the grid with a visible marker in the headers; Ctrl+9, Ctrl+0 and Ctrl+Shift+9 work, and selecting across a hidden range then Unhide shows it again.
Saved files keep sizes and hidden state as standard <col>/<row> attributes and reopen in Excel and LibreOffice identically; files opened with hidden or custom-sized columns display them correctly.
Playwright tests cover drag, double-click AutoFit, the Format menu, hide/unhide shortcuts, undo and save round-trip; Cells stays two rows; bundle-budget and all required checks green.

proposals.headline: Review tab with Track Changes: see redlines, then accept or reject them one by one
proposals.today_caption: Today (a sample term sheet with 11 tracked changes by two reviewers, opened in the live demo): Nitro paints deleted and inserted text run together with no markup, so the facility reads "USD 250,000,000USD 300,000,000" and the term "threefive years". There is no Review tab, so changes cannot be seen, accepted or rejected.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: a Review tab (Tracking: Track Changes on, All Markup, Reviewing Pane; Changes: Accept, Reject, Previous, Next). Deletions are struck through and insertions underlined in each reviewer's colour, with change bars in the margin, a revisions list with Accept / Reject, and 'Track Changes: On' in the status bar.
proposals.why: Redlined drafts are how contracts, term sheets and policies move between people, and today Nitro shows them wrongly: the old and the new text appear side by side as if both were current, which is worse than not opening the file. Word, Google Docs (Suggesting), OnlyOffice and Collabora all show markup and accept/reject. Nitro's Word engine already models w:ins / w:del and has accept and reject (ported in #82), so this is mainly painting the markup and adding the Review tab.
proposals.effort_note: 3–5 days (paint insertions/deletions/format changes in author colours with change bars; All Markup / Simple Markup / No Markup / Original views; Review tab with Track Changes toggle, Accept / Reject (this, all shown, all), Previous / Next; revisions pane; typing while tracking writes w:ins/w:del with author and date from a host-set user name). Comments (declined in #578) stay out of scope.
proposals.risk: Medium. Markup changes layout (struck text still takes space), so pagination must use the same view the user picked. Accept/reject must write the same XML Word does and keep untouched revisions byte-identical. The Review tab is a new tab; the Home tab, including Font and Paragraph at two rows, is unchanged.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: Review tab and pane are a lazy chunk (a few KB). Painting markup reuses the existing run painter with extra decoration; documents without revisions pay nothing. A 200-page document with 1,000 revisions must still open within today's budget.
dod: Documents with tracked changes show insertions underlined and deletions struck through in per-author colours with change bars; No Markup and Original show the final and original text correctly (never both run together).

A Review tab has Track Changes (toggle), All Markup / Simple Markup / No Markup / Original, Reviewing Pane, Accept and Reject (this change, all shown, all) and Previous / Next; each accept/reject is one undo step.
With Track Changes on, typing and deleting write w:ins / w:del with the author (host-settable, e.g. a user attribute or React prop) and the date; the status bar shows Track Changes: On.
Saved files open in Word and LibreOffice with the same revisions; accepted/rejected results match Word's; untouched revisions round-trip byte-identical.

Playwright tests cover rendering, each view, accept/reject one and all, tracked typing and save round-trip; Home ribbon unchanged (Font and Paragraph two rows); bundle-budget and all required checks green.

proposals.headline: Open huge workbooks straight from storage: fetch only the bytes on screen, stream the rest, no size wall
proposals.today_label: TODAY · from code and measured data
proposals.today_caption: Today: loadUrl() downloads every byte (fetch, then arrayBuffer) before parsing starts, and files over 50 MiB compressed are refused with "Package too large." The engine itself is fast: 48.7 ms to the first view of a 17.2 MB workbook.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: the host preview paints the first screen after fetching only the zip directory, workbook, styles and the visible row blocks with HTTP Range requests; the rest streams in a worker or on scroll, with progress and Cancel.
proposals.why: Big-workbook previews are where Nitro can beat everyone, and that is the case Jared's company has: very large Excel files on AWS EFS, previewed in a React app. Parsing is already fast (Nitro's engine shows the first view of a 17.2 MB workbook in 48.7 ms; the TypeScript engine it replaced takes 5,069 ms). The bottleneck now is the network and a size cap: every byte must arrive before parsing starts, and anything over 50 MiB is refused. This bet removes both. Nitro reads the zip directory with HTTP Range requests, fetches only the parts and rows on screen, streams the rest in a worker, and keeps memory flat on million-row sheets.
proposals.wins: Embedding developers first: preview panes in React and host apps over S3, CloudFront, or EFS behind a web server, where today the whole file crosses the network before anything shows. Then every user who opens a big workbook. Today Nitro is fast once the bytes arrive. This bet makes it fast from the moment the file is requested, with no file-size ceiling for URL sources.

phases.name: M1 · Range-request open (about 1 week)
phases.ships: loadUrl / src reads the zip central directory with HTTP Range and fetches only workbook, styles, shared strings and the first visible sheet. If the server ignores Range or CORS hides Content-Range, it falls back to today's full download. This milestone already helps any Range-capable store on its own.

phases.name: M2 · Streaming first view in a worker (1–2 weeks)
phases.ships: The visible sheet is inflated and parsed in row blocks as bytes arrive. The first screen paints from the first blocks, and load progress / ready / cancel events fire (absorbs proposal #614).

phases.name: M3 · Million-row grid with flat memory (1–2 weeks)
phases.ships: A row-block cache with eviction keeps memory bounded on a 1,048,576-row sheet, and jumping to any row fetches only that block. The 50 MiB cap is lifted for streamed URL sources only. In-memory buffers keep the cap, and the zip-bomb and ratio guards stay unchanged.

phases.name: M4 · React + storage recipe (3–5 days)
phases.ships: <NitroViewer src preview> in React, a docs recipe for S3 presigned URLs and EFS behind nginx/CloudFront, and a throttled-network row in the browser perf table.

evidence.text: First view of the 17.2 MB XL workbook: 48.7 ms in Nitro's engine vs 5,069 ms in the TS engine. Peak memory 44.6 MiB vs 1,682.7 MiB.
Browser first paint of that workbook: 399 ms median, 658 ms p95, served from localhost. Network time on a real store is not in these numbers yet.
URL loads download the whole file before parsing: fetch(url), then arrayBuffer(), then loadBuffer().
Inputs over 50 MiB compressed throw input_too_large, which users see as "Package too large."
#210 (closed) made parsing lazy per sheet and viewport-only. Byte-range access was in its spec, but URL loading still reads everything.
Demand: Jared's company previews very large Excel files from AWS EFS in a React app. Proposal #614 (load progress / ready / cancel) is open.
For comparison, Google Sheets caps a spreadsheet at 10 million cells and converts xlsx into its own format to edit it. Excel's grid is 1,048,576 rows × 16,384 columns.
evidence.source: Google Sheets and Microsoft Excel published limits

proposals.effort_note: Multi-week: about 4–6 weeks over 4 milestones, each shippable alone
proposals.risk: Medium to high. Zip parts are deflate-compressed, so a sheet's rows can only be read in order from the start of its part. Random access to row 900,000 may mean streaming the bytes before it once and caching block offsets. Servers without Range support, or with CORS that hides Content-Range, need a clean fallback. The zip-bomb and ratio guards must hold for each streamed part.
proposals.perf: Goal: time to first screen depends on the bytes shown, not on file size, and memory stays flat while scrolling 1M rows. The Range reader and stream glue go in a new lazy chunk loaded only for URL sources. The eager loader must stay under 17,408 B brotli. Draft PR #621's branch measured 17,159 B, so the loader change can only be a tiny lazy import.
dod: Opening a 200 MB or larger xlsx by URL from a Range-capable test server paints the first screen without downloading the whole file. A CI test checks that bytes fetched before first paint are 10% of the file or less, and that first paint is 1.5 s or less at a 'Fast 4G' throttle.
Servers without Range support fall back to today's full download with identical output. Zip-bomb, ratio and part-size guards still trip.
Scrolling or jumping to row 1,000,000 of a 1M-row sheet fetches only the blocks it needs, and a memory CI keeps the heap within a fixed budget.
React <NitroViewer src> preview mode plus docs for S3 presigned URLs and EFS behind nginx. Load progress / ready / cancel events work (#614).
Eager loader under 17,408 B brotli. docs/perf gains a throttled-network row. All required checks green.
proposals.status_note: Approved 2026-11-24 (👍). Strategic multi-milestone bet; queued for the nightly build behind host-API priority work. Build lands as phased draft PRs (milestone 1 first).

proposals.headline: Open long Word documents in about a second: page 1 first, the rest laid out in the background, only visible pages kept in memory
proposals.today_caption: Today (measured): a 200-slide deck and a 1M-cell workbook paint in about 260 ms, a 500-page Word document takes 980 ms, and the 11.8 MB XL document did not paint within 90 s in 5 of 5 runs.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: page 1 shows right away; the page rail fills in as layout continues in the background; the status bar says the page count is still counting; only pages near the screen stay in memory.
proposals.why: Contracts, reports and manuals often run to hundreds of pages, and Word is Nitro's slowest format. A 500-page document takes 980 ms to first paint, against 266 ms for a 1M-cell workbook. The 11.8 MB XL document never painted within 90 seconds. The engine numbers point to work that grows with document length before page 1 appears: 449.8 ms to open the 500-page file, against 9.7 ms for the large workbook. Word and PDF viewers show the first page and keep laying out the rest. This bet does the same, then keeps memory flat and makes editing a long document cheap.
proposals.wins: Users first: anyone opening a long contract, thesis or report. Then embedding developers whose apps preview Word attachments (document review, AI chat over files), where one large .docx must never freeze the tab. This closes Nitro's only large-file gap: Excel and PowerPoint already beat the TS engine by 100× or more at the large tiers.

phases.name: M1 · Profile + page 1 first (about 1 week)
phases.ships: Profile pages_500.docx and xl_a.docx to find what blocks first paint. Lay out and paint the first screenful of pages before the rest. 'Page 1 of …' counts up as layout continues.

phases.name: M2 · Background layout off the main thread (1–2 weeks)
phases.ships: Pagination continues in the worker in time-sliced batches, so scrolling and typing stay responsive. Scrolling to a page that isn't laid out yet jumps to an estimated position and settles once that page is ready.

phases.name: M3 · Page virtualization (about 1 week)
phases.ships: Only pages near the viewport keep their DOM or canvas. The rest are light placeholders at the right height, so memory stays flat past 1,000 pages.

phases.name: M4 · Incremental re-layout on edit (1–2 weeks)
phases.ships: Typing re-lays out from the edited paragraph only until page breaks settle, so editing page 300 never touches pages 1–299.

evidence.text: docx XL (xl_a.docx, 11,773,330 B): the browser render did not complete within 90 s in 5 of 5 runs.
Browser first paint (median): docx L (pages_500.docx) 980 ms; xlsx L (cells_1m.xlsx) 266 ms; pptx L (slides_200.pptx) 261 ms.

Engine cold open, L tier: docx 449.75 ms, xlsx 9.73 ms, pptx 6.69 ms. Against the TS engine, docx L improves only 2.5× (ratio 0.401); xlsx L and pptx L improve about 160–200× (ratios 0.006 and 0.005).
Peak memory: docx L 209.0 MiB vs xlsx L 22.7 MiB.
Large docx is already causing problems: #550 (the TS oracle can't open docx XL) and a docx_load memory-cut branch (Part of #30). Issue #23 (Print Layout painter) is still open.
How others do it: desktop Word paginates in the background (the page count grows as it works), and PDF viewers show page 1 before the rest of the document has loaded.

proposals.effort_note: Multi-week: about 4–6 weeks over 4 milestones, each shippable alone
proposals.risk: High in places. Each page break depends on everything before it (widow and orphan control, keep-with-next, floating objects, section breaks, footnotes), so background layout must end up with exactly today's pagination. A page-count and pixel parity test on every docx fixture guards that. PAGE and NUMPAGES fields and TOC page numbers show estimates until layout finishes.
proposals.perf: Goal: page 1 paints in under 1 s at every docx tier, including XL, and memory stays flat beyond the visible pages. Layout scheduling lives in Rust/WASM. Placeholders and virtualization live in the lazy Word chunk. No new eager JS; the loader stays under 17,408 B brotli.
dod: browser-e2e: docx XL (xl_a.docx) paints page 1 in 1 s median or less (today: nothing within 90 s), and docx L in 400 ms or less, published in docs/perf.
Once background layout finishes, page count and per-page pixels match today's full layout on every docx fixture.
Scrolling a 1,000-page document keeps the heap within a fixed budget (memory CI), and the status bar shows 'Page X of Y', updating as layout continues.
Typing on page 300 re-lays out only from that paragraph forward, and the docx edit perf gate stays green.
Eager loader under 17,408 B brotli. All required checks green.
proposals.status_note: Approved 2026-11-24 (👍). Strategic multi-milestone bet; queued for the nightly build behind host-API priority work. Build lands as phased draft PRs (milestone 1 first).

proposals.headline: PivotTables: show them as real pivots, refresh them, and build new ones from a field list
proposals.today_caption: Today: the corpus file poi-ExcelPivotTableSample.xlsx (sheet Tabelle3) opens with its pivot as plain cells, with no pivot styling, field buttons or filter dropdown, and no way to refresh it or make a new one.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: the same pivot painted as a pivot (header band, grand-total row, filter and row-label dropdowns), a PivotTable tab, and a PivotTable Fields pane with Filters / Columns / Rows / Values areas, Refresh and Insert PivotTable.
proposals.why: PivotTables are how most Excel users summarise data, and every serious competitor has them: Excel, Google Sheets, OnlyOffice and LibreOffice/Collabora. Nitro keeps pivots intact on save, but shows them as plain cells. The engine's own warning says they are 'kept on save but are not refreshed or shown as pivot tables'. The formula engine and dependency graph already exist to compute the aggregates. This bet makes pivots first-class in three shippable steps, then opens them to host apps so an AI assistant can build a summary the user can inspect and save.
proposals.wins: Users first: analysts, finance and ops teams, the same people who open the big workbooks. Then embedding developers: an agent asked for 'total by region' can create a real, refreshable pivot instead of pasting static numbers. Pivots are the largest everyday Excel feature Nitro doesn't have yet.

phases.name: M1 · Show pivots faithfully (about 1 week)
phases.ships: Read pivotTable and pivotCache parts, then paint pivot styles, row and column headers, subtotals, grand totals, field buttons and the page-filter '(Multiple Items)' dropdown. Read-only.

phases.name: M2 · Refresh, filter, expand and collapse (1–2 weeks)
phases.ships: Recompute from the worksheet source (Sum, Count, Average, Min, Max), with field filters and collapsible groups. Save writes cache records that Excel opens without a repair prompt.

phases.name: M3 · Insert PivotTable + field list (about 2 weeks)
phases.ships: Insert > PivotTable from a selected range (reusing the Insert tab from approved #606), a PivotTable Fields pane with Filters / Columns / Rows / Values areas, drag to rearrange, live update, one undo step per change.

phases.name: M4 · Host API for pivots (3–5 days)
phases.ships: getPivots(), applyEdit ops pivot.create and pivot.set-fields, and a nitro-pivot-change event, typed and documented for AI agents.

evidence.text: Today: poi-ExcelPivotTableSample.xlsx (in the test corpus) shows its pivot on Tabelle3 as plain cells (screenshot above, live demo at v0.2.0, taken 2026-11-24).
The engine warns on open: 'Pivot tables are kept on save but are not refreshed or shown as pivot tables.'
The calculation base exists: formula parser, dependency graph and function library (#71–#77, all closed).
No existing issue or proposal covers pivots. Approved #606 (Insert tab + charts) and #577 (Sort & Filter) add the Insert tab and filter UI this bet reuses.
Competitors: Excel, Google Sheets, OnlyOffice and LibreOffice/Collabora all create and refresh pivot tables.

proposals.effort_note: Multi-week: about 5–7 weeks over 4 milestones, each shippable alone
proposals.risk: Medium to high. The pivot XML model is large (definitions, caches, records, styles, OLAP and Data Model pivots). M1–M2 cover worksheet-source pivots only and keep everything else read-only with a clear note. Saved files must open in Excel without a repair prompt, which the existing round-trip and validator CI enforces.
proposals.perf: Aggregation runs in Rust over cache records. Target: refresh of a 1M-row source in under 1 s, measured in CI on generated data. The pivot UI and field list go in a new lazy chunk loaded only when a workbook has pivots or the user inserts one. No first-load growth; the eager loader stays under 17,408 B brotli.
dod: poi-ExcelPivotTableSample.xlsx and the other corpus pivots render with pivot style, headers, totals, field buttons and filter dropdowns, checked by a pixel test against an Excel-rendered reference.
Refresh recomputes after source edits, and filter and collapse work. The saved file opens in Excel with no repair prompt and refreshes to the same values.
Insert > PivotTable on a range opens the field list. Dragging fields between Filters, Columns, Rows and Values updates the pivot live, and Ctrl+Z undoes each change.
Host API: getPivots(), pivot.create and pivot.set-fields ops, and a nitro-pivot-change event, typed and documented.
Ribbon groups stay at 2 rows or fewer. Eager loader under 17,408 B brotli. All required checks green.

proposals.headline: Conditional Formatting: data bars, colour scales and highlight rules, with live preview
proposals.today_caption: Today (F11:F22 selected): Nitro already paints conditional formats that come in the file (the red-to-green colour scale on rows 1–10), but the Home tab has no way to add, change or remove one.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: a Styles group on Home with Conditional Formatting. Hovering Data Bars › blue previews bars on the selection; a 'Greater Than 140' highlight rule shades column H. Rules save as standard Excel conditional formatting.
proposals.why: Conditional formatting is how people actually read a sheet of numbers: outliers in red, a heat map, bars that show size at a glance. Excel, Google Sheets, OnlyOffice and Collabora all have it on the main toolbar. Nitro already renders these rules when a file has them, so adding the authoring side mostly means writing the same XML the painter already reads.
proposals.effort_note: 3–4 days (Styles group button + menu; Highlight Cells Rules (greater/less/between/equal/text contains/duplicates), Top/Bottom (top 10, above average), Data Bars, Color Scales, Icon Sets presets; live preview on hover; Clear Rules from selection/sheet; simple Manage Rules list; one undo step per rule)

proposals.perf: No first-load change: menu and dialog live in the lazily loaded Excel ribbon chunk (a few KB). The painter already evaluates rules; live preview re-paints only the visible selection.
dod: Home > Styles has Conditional Formatting with Highlight Cells Rules, Top/Bottom Rules, Data Bars, Color Scales, Icon Sets, New Rule…, Clear Rules and Manage Rules…

proposals.headline: Line shapes up: smart guides while dragging, plus Align and Distribute
proposals.today_caption: Today (slide 2, dragging the third card's text box): no guides appear and nothing snaps, so it is easy to drop a shape a few pixels off. The Arrange group has order and group buttons but no Align or Distribute.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: while dragging, red dashed smart guides show when the card's top, middle or bottom line up with the others, and equal-gap markers show the spacing matches. A new Align menu in Arrange offers Align Left/Center/Right/Top/Middle/Bottom and Distribute.

proposals.headline: Let host apps highlight cells, text or shapes (for example AI citations) without touching the file
proposals.today_caption: Today (embedded workbook): a host can move the selection or edit cell formatting, but has no way to mark a range temporarily. Pointing at 'B11:B20' means stealing the user's selection or dirtying the file.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: the host's chat panel cites two ranges. Nitro paints them as numbered, coloured highlights over the grid (B11:B20 amber, E14:G14 violet), with a hover card. The user's own selection (A1) is untouched and the file stays 'No changes'.
proposals.why: When Nitro sits inside a chat app with an AI agent, the agent's answers point at specific cells, sentences or shapes, and users need to see exactly what it means. Today the only tools are the selection (which the user owns) and real formatting (which changes the file). A highlight layer that is never saved is how code editors (decorations) and PDF viewers (annotations) solve this, and it reuses the getSelection/setPosition addresses Nitro already has.
proposals.effort_note: 2–4 days (setHighlights/clearHighlights/revealHighlight on the element and the React handle; xlsx range overlay in the grid layer; docx text-range and pptx shape overlays using the same address formats as getSelection; nitro-highlight-click event; stays aligned on scroll, zoom, frozen panes, reload in place)
proposals.risk: Low to medium. Read-only overlay, never written to the file and never part of undo, so no round-trip risk. The main risk is overlays drifting from the painted content after edits, zoom or reflow; ranges that no longer exist must drop cleanly and say so.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: overlay code lives in the existing per-format shells, a few KB. Painting is a DOM/canvas overlay redrawn on scroll; a test keeps 200 highlights under one frame. The loader stays under its 17,408 B budget.
dod: el.setHighlights([{ id, range | textRange | shapeId, color, label }]) paints numbered highlights in xlsx (ranges, any sheet), docx (text ranges from getSelection/scrollToText) and pptx (shapes); clearHighlights() and per-id removal work.
revealHighlight(id) scrolls/switches sheet, page or slide to show it without changing the user's selection or focus.
Clicking a highlight fires nitro-highlight-click with its id; React exposes the same via the handle and an onHighlightClick prop.
Highlights are never saved, never mark the document dirty (el.dirty stays false, save() bytes unchanged) and survive reload(bytes) when their address is still valid.
Playwright tests cover all three formats, zoom, frozen panes and reload; TypeScript types and README section added; bundle-budget and all required checks green.
proposals.status_note: Approved 2026-11-24 (👍). Queued for the nightly build behind host-API priority work and #612.

proposals.headline: Range selection that keeps up with your mouse, like Excel
proposals.today_caption: Today (B12:E19 dragged): the range gets an outline but no shading. Clicking a column or row header does not select it, dragging past the bottom edge does not auto-scroll, and there is no size tip or Ctrl+click second range.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: a shaded range with the active cell left white, a second Ctrl+click range (G14:H17), a size tip (8R × 4C) at the pointer, edge auto-scroll, and header click to select whole columns or rows. A CI test holds pointer-to-paint to one frame.
proposals.why: Jared's comment on #606: range selection feels less responsive than Excel, as in many open-source editors, and it is a part of the experience he wants Nitro to do really well. Selecting is the first step of almost every Excel action (format, chart, sum, copy). Excel and Google Sheets shade the range, select whole columns and rows from the headers, auto-scroll at the edges and paint on the next frame. Light probe on main ee9789c: header click and edge auto-scroll do nothing today; drag, Shift+click, Shift+Arrow and Ctrl+A already work.
proposals.effort_note: 2–4 days (selection painted as a main-thread overlay updated every animation frame, with no wait on the worker; shaded fill; header click/drag/Shift+click for columns and rows; Ctrl+click multi-range in the model and getSelection; edge auto-scroll with speed by distance; size tip; latency trace test). Ctrl+Arrow jumps stay with #519.
proposals.risk: Medium. Multi-range selection touches copy, Clear, formatting and getSelection, which must act on all ranges or say clearly that they cannot. The overlay must stay pixel-aligned with the painted grid at every zoom and with frozen panes (#547).
proposals.perf: Selection should get cheaper: drag updates a lightweight overlay each frame instead of repainting the grid. No first-load change; the code lives in the existing Excel shell. The loader stays under 17,408 B.
dod: Dragging, Shift+click and Shift+Arrow paint a shaded range (active cell white) and update the Name Box on the next animation frame; a Playwright trace test on a 100k-row sheet holds pointer-to-paint p95 ≤ 16 ms at 1×–4× CPU throttle.
Clicking a column or row header selects it; dragging across headers or Shift+clicking selects many; the corner button and Ctrl+A select all.
Dragging past any edge auto-scrolls, faster the further the pointer goes, and stops when the pointer comes back inside.
Ctrl/Cmd+click and Ctrl+drag add ranges; Clear, Bold, number formats and copy apply to every range; getSelection reports all ranges.
A size tip (for example 8R × 4C) follows the pointer while dragging; Font, Alignment and Number groups stay at two rows; bundle-budget and all required checks green.

proposals.headline: AutoSum (Σ, Alt+=): total a column in one click, with Average, Count, Max and Min
proposals.today_caption: Today: the Editing group on Excel's Home tab has only Clear and Find. To total a column you must type =SUM( and the range by hand, and Alt+= does nothing.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: AutoSum (Σ) in Home > Editing with a menu of Sum, Average, Count Numbers, Max and Min. It proposes =SUM(B1:B10) and shows the range dashed so you can adjust it before pressing Enter.
proposals.why: AutoSum is one of the most-used buttons in Excel and the quickest way to a total. Excel, Google Sheets (Σ Functions), OnlyOffice and Collabora all have it. Nitro already calculates SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, MAX and MIN, so this is a small change that removes a lot of typing.
proposals.effort_note: 1–2 days (Editing group button with menu, range guess: contiguous numbers above, else left, stopping at blanks/text and existing totals; Alt+=; block selection fills a total row/column; uses the existing formula engine and one undo step)
proposals.risk: Low. Only writes ordinary formulas. The range guess must match Excel (stop at the first blank or text cell, skip a header row) so users are not surprised. Font, Alignment and Number groups are unchanged and stay at two rows.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: a few KB in the lazily loaded Excel ribbon chunk. Recalc reuses the existing session calculator.
dod: Home > Editing shows AutoSum (Σ) with a split menu: Sum, Average, Count Numbers, Max, Min; Alt+= runs Sum.
On a single cell it proposes the contiguous numbers above (else to the left) as =SUM(range), shows the range dashed, and Enter commits; Esc cancels.
With a block selected (for example B1:E10), it writes totals in the row below (or column to the right) for every column in one undo step.
Formulas save with <f> and cached <v> and reopen in Excel and LibreOffice with the same values.

Playwright tests cover the range guess (blank stop, header skip, left fallback), each function, block totals, undo and save round-trip; Font, Alignment and Number groups stay at two rows; bundle-budget and all required checks green.

proposals.headline: Let host apps show load progress, know when a big file is viewable, and cancel it
proposals.today_caption: Today: while a workbook opens, the host can only show an indeterminate spinner. The element fires no progress, no 'first sheet is on screen' signal and no load error event, and loadUrl cannot be cancelled.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: the host shows a real progress bar and a toast with Cancel. Sheet1 is scrollable as soon as nitro-ready fires while the remaining sheets keep loading. The event log on the right shows the proposed events.
proposals.why: Big workbooks are where Nitro has to feel fast, for example in previews of large Excel files kept on shared storage. Today the host cannot tell 'still unzipping' from 'hung', cannot say 'first sheet ready', and cannot stop a 40 MB open when the user clicks away. Embedding APIs from OnlyOffice (onAppReady / onDocumentReady / onError) and Collabora (App_LoadingStatus: Frame_Ready, Document_Loaded) both expose these milestones.
proposals.effort_note: 1–2 days (forward the worker's existing open phases as nitro-loadstart / nitro-progress / nitro-ready / nitro-load / nitro-error, an AbortSignal option on loadUrl/loadBuffer/loadFile, typed details in index.d.ts, React onProgress/onReady/onLoad/onError props, README section)
proposals.risk: Low. The events are additive and read-only. Progress is throttled to at most one event per animation frame so it never slows parsing. Abort must free the worker and keep the previous document on screen, which the reload() work already does.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: a few hundred bytes in the loader (well under the 17,408 B eager budget). Events are posted from phases the worker already runs; no extra parsing or copying.
dod: <nitro-docx>, <nitro-xlsx> and <nitro-pptx> fire nitro-loadstart {name, bytes}, nitro-progress {phase, loaded, total} (at most once per frame), nitro-ready when the first page/sheet/slide is painted, nitro-load when everything is loaded, and nitro-error {code, message} for password-protected, corrupt and over-limit files.
loadUrl, loadBuffer and loadFile accept {signal}; abort() rejects with AbortError, frees the worker and keeps the previous document and position.
Typed event details in loader/index.d.ts and React props onProgress, onReady, onLoad and onError on <NitroViewer>; documented in the loader README with a copy-paste host example.
Events never fire for reload() with keepPosition unless asked, never mark the document dirty and never move focus.
Browser e2e test in demo/host-api covers event order, abort mid-load and each error code on an L-tier workbook; bundle-budget and all required checks green.

proposals.headline: Turn a selected range into a chart, from a new Insert tab
proposals.today_caption: Today: Excel has only File, Home and View. There is no Insert tab and no way to make a chart, so a selected range of numbers (A1:D6 here) stays a range of numbers.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: a new Insert tab with Insert Chart. The gallery offers Column, Bar, Line and Pie; a clustered column chart of A1:D6 lands on the sheet as a movable object.
proposals.why: You can already open a workbook that contains a chart — the painter shipped in M1 — but you cannot make one. Excel, Google Sheets, OnlyOffice and Collabora all put Insert Chart next to the selection. Nitro has no Insert tab on Excel today, so a range of numbers stays a range of numbers.
proposals.effort_note: 3–4 days (Insert tab with a Charts group, gallery of clustered column/bar/line/pie, write a standard chart part and two-cell anchor from one contiguous range, reuse the existing chart painter, move/resize, one undo, save round-trip)
proposals.risk: Medium. Chart XML (chart part, colours, cached values, drawing anchor) must reopen in Excel and LibreOffice without repair, and the cache must match the range so Excel does not prompt to update. Out of scope: combo charts, secondary axes, pivot charts and chart sheets.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: the Insert tab and gallery load with a lazily loaded Excel ribbon chunk (a few KB). Painting reuses the existing chart painter. The loader stays under 17,408 B.
dod: Excel gains an Insert tab (File, Home, Insert, View) with a Charts group; Insert Chart opens a gallery of Column, Bar, Line and Pie.
With a contiguous range of numbers selected, choosing a type inserts a chart object on the sheet, titled from the range, with a legend; the range remains the source.
The chart is one undo step, can be moved and resized, and is saved as standard chart and drawing parts; files reopen in Excel and LibreOffice without repair and still paint in Nitro.
Editing a source cell updates the chart after the edit is committed.
Playwright tests cover each type, undo, move, save round-trip and OOXML/LibreOffice validation; Font, Alignment and Number groups stay at two rows; bundle-budget and all required checks green.

proposals.headline: Jump to any heading from a Navigation pane
proposals.today_caption: Today: View has only Zoom and Diagnostics. Headings are in the page, but there is no list of them, so you scroll to find a section. Ctrl+F opens a find box that does not even focus the search field.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: View > Navigation (or Ctrl+F) opens a left pane with Headings, Pages and Results. The heading on screen is highlighted; click one to jump to it.
proposals.why: Word, Google Docs (the document outline) and OnlyOffice all offer a headings list so you can jump around a long document without scrolling. Nitro already paginates and knows paragraph styles (Title, Heading 1–3), and v0.2.0 added get/setPosition, so a jump is a scroll, not a new layout engine. Ctrl+F today opens a find box that does not focus the search field; this puts Find in a Navigation pane with Headings, Pages and Results, the way Word does.
proposals.effort_note: 1–2 days (Navigation button on View, heading walk from styles, click-to-scroll, Pages list, Results reuses today's find and focuses the box, Ctrl+F)
proposals.risk: Low. The pane is read-mostly and does not change the file. Headings without a heading style are omitted, as in Word's outline. Navigation is one button in the existing Show group on View, so Font and Paragraph stay at two rows.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: a few KB in the lazily loaded Word chrome chunk. The heading list is built from the already-loaded document model; jump uses the existing scroll and position APIs. The loader stays under 17,408 B.
dod: View > Navigation (pressed while open) shows a left pane with Headings, Pages and Results; Ctrl+F opens it on Results with the search box focused.
Headings lists Title and Heading 1–3 in document order, indents by level, and highlights the heading currently on screen; click or Enter scrolls that heading into view and moves the caret.
The list updates after typing, style changes and undo; an empty document or a document with no headings shows a short empty state.
Pages lists one row per page and jumps to that page. Results is today's find (replace stays with #542) inside the same pane.
Playwright tests cover open/close, click-to-jump, keyboard, empty state and focused search; Font and Paragraph stay at two rows; bundle-budget and all required checks green.

proposals.headline: See every slide at once and drag to reorder, in Slide Sorter view
proposals.today_caption: Today: View has Zoom, a Slide pane toggle and Previous/Next. The only way to see the deck is the narrow left rail in Normal view, so checking the flow or reordering several slides means a lot of scrolling and Move Slide Up/Down.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: View > Slide Sorter fills the canvas with a grid of every slide, with number and title. The current slide is outlined; drag a slide to reorder, double-click to return to Normal.
proposals.why: PowerPoint's Slide Sorter is how people check the flow of a deck and reorder several slides at a glance. Nitro already paints thumbnails for the left rail and already has Move Slide Up/Down, but View has no sorter, so you only ever see one big slide plus a narrow strip. This is a layout of those thumbs, plus drag-to-reorder. It is not a slide show (that remains deferred).
proposals.effort_note: 2–3 days (View > Slide Sorter and Normal, a wrapping thumbnail grid, click to select, drag to reorder, Delete and Ctrl+D, double-click or Escape to return, save keeps the new order)
proposals.risk: Low. Reorder is the same operation as today's Move Slide Up/Down, as one undo step. Hidden slides, if any, stay hidden but remain in the grid, as PowerPoint does. This must not invent a slide-show or presenter view.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: a few KB in the lazily loaded PowerPoint chrome chunk. Thumbnails already rendered for the rail are reused. The loader stays under 17,408 B.
dod: View > Slide Sorter (and a Normal button) switches the canvas to a grid of all slides at a readable size, with slide number and title; the current slide is outlined.
Drag-and-drop reorders slides; Delete removes the selected slide; Ctrl+D duplicates it; each change is one undo step and survives save.
Click selects; double-click, View > Normal or Escape returns to Normal on that slide; arrow keys and Previous/Next move the selection.

proposals.headline: Colour cells, add borders and Merge & Center from Excel's Home tab
proposals.today_caption: Today: Excel Home > Font has Bold, Italic, Underline, Strikethrough and font size only. There is no Borders, Fill Color or Font Color, and Alignment has no Merge & Center, so you can't format a simple table.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: Borders, Fill Color and Font Color split buttons join the two-row Font group, and Merge & Center joins Alignment. The Borders menu is open; B12:F15 shows a merged, filled title row and All Borders.
proposals.why: Borders, fill colour, font colour and Merge & Center are the most-used buttons on Excel's Home tab, and Google Sheets, OnlyOffice and Collabora all put them in the same place. Nitro already paints fills, borders and merged cells that arrive in a file, the style writer already pools fills and borders, and the command ids (home.borders, home.fill-color, home.font-color, home.merge-center) are registered. But none of them are on the ribbon or wired to an edit, so you can't turn a range of numbers into a readable table.
proposals.effort_note: 2–3 days (ribbon split buttons and palettes, three style edits plus merge/unmerge on the existing writer, undo, save round-trip)
proposals.risk: Low to medium. New fills and borders must dedupe into styles.xml (no style explosion on repeated clicks), and mergeCells must stay valid: merging over data keeps only the top-left value, with Excel's warning. Font group stays at two rows: the three new split buttons replace no existing control.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: palettes and the Borders menu load with the lazily loaded Excel ribbon chunk (a few KB). Each click is one style edit on the selection; painting fills and borders already exists.
dod: Home > Font gains Borders, Fill Color and Font Color split buttons (last-used colour on the face, palette with theme and standard colours plus No Fill / Automatic); the Font group stays at two rows.
Borders menu offers Bottom, Top, Left, Right, No Border, All Borders, Outside Borders and Thick Box Border; each applies to the selection as one undo step.
Home > Alignment gains Merge & Center with Merge Across, Merge Cells and Unmerge Cells; merging over data keeps the top-left value and warns first, as Excel does.
Saved files reopen in Excel and LibreOffice without repair, with fills, borders, font colours and merges intact; repeated formatting reuses existing styles.xml entries (validator + round-trip in CI).
Playwright tests cover each border type, fill, font colour, merge/unmerge, undo and a save round-trip; bundle-budget and all required checks green; no first-load size limit raised.

proposals.headline: Format Painter and Clear Formatting: copy a look in one click, or wipe it
proposals.today_caption: Today: Home > Clipboard has Cut, Copy and Paste only. There is no Format Painter, and Home > Font has no Clear All Formatting button, so matching or resetting a look means redoing each setting by hand.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: Format Painter in Clipboard (pressed) and Clear All Formatting in Font row 1. The look of “What we shipped” is copied, then painted onto a bullet line with the brush cursor.
proposals.why: Format Painter is one of the most-used buttons in all three Office apps, and Google Docs, Sheets and Slides (paint format), OnlyOffice and Collabora (Clone Formatting) all have it. Today, making one heading, cell or text box look like another means repeating font, size, colour and alignment by hand, and there is no one-click way back to plain text. The command ids (home.format-painter, home.clear-formats) are already registered; this wires them to the selection with one shared implementation across Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
proposals.effort_note: 2–3 days (capture/apply of run + paragraph properties in Word and PowerPoint, cell style in Excel; brush cursor and sticky mode; Clear Formatting)
proposals.risk: Low. Painting is a normal formatting edit of the target, so it reuses existing run, paragraph and cell-style writers and is one undo step. Edge cases: painting a paragraph mark copies paragraph formatting (as Word does); Excel paints over a range by size; Esc must cancel sticky mode and leave focus in the document.
proposals.perf: No first-load change and a few KB in each lazy ribbon chunk. Capture is a read of the current selection; apply is one edit.
dod: Home > Clipboard gains Format Painter in all three apps; single click paints once, double click stays on until Esc or a second click; Ctrl+Shift+C / Ctrl+Shift+V copy and paste formatting.

Word and PowerPoint: copies character formatting (font, size, bold/italic/underline, colour, highlight) and, when the source includes the paragraph mark, paragraph formatting; Excel copies the full cell style (number format, font, fill, borders, alignment) to the painted range.
Home > Font gains Clear All Formatting (Word/PowerPoint: back to the paragraph style's defaults; Excel: Clear Formats) without adding a ribbon row.
Each paint or clear is one undo step and survives save; files reopen in Office and LibreOffice without repair.

proposals.headline: Let host apps hide, add and run ribbon commands (ribbon option, execCommand, nitro-command event)
proposals.today_caption: Today: an embedding app gets the full or embedded toolbar as-is. It can't hide Open or Insert Picture, can't add its own “Send for review” button, and has no public way to run a command like Bold from its own UI.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: the host hid Open and added “Insert clause” and “Send for review” to the embedded toolbar. Clicking a host button fires nitro-command; the code card shows the ribbon option and execCommand.
proposals.why: Every host that embeds an editor wants to trim commands it doesn't support (Open, Save As, Insert Picture) and add one or two of its own (Send for review, Insert clause, Submit). OnlyOffice and Collabora both expose this through their integration APIs. Nitro already has a single command registry shared by the ribbon and shortcuts (ids like home.bold, file.open, insert.picture), so exposing it as a small, typed host API is cheap. It also fixes the stringly typed applyEdit gap in #531 for the common case.
proposals.effort_note: 2–3 days (ribbon option on the element and React prop, hide/add in both toolbar modes, execCommand + typed id union, nitro-command event, docs)
proposals.risk: Low to medium. Command ids become public API, so they need a stable, documented list (generated from the registry) and a guard test. Host buttons must respect readonly and keyboard focus order, and must never inject HTML: label and icon are text and SVG path data only, which keeps the strict-CSP goal in #573.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: the option is read when the ribbon is first built, and hidden commands are simply not rendered. execCommand dispatches through the existing registry. No new chunk.
dod: el.ribbon = { hide: [...ids], add: [{ id, label, icon?, tab?, group?, primary?, menu? }] } (and a React ribbon prop) works in full and embedded modes. Hidden ids vanish from ribbon, menus and shortcuts; added buttons appear in the named tab/group, or at the end of the embedded toolbar.

el.execCommand(id, args?) runs any registered command with a typed id union in index.d.ts and returns false (with the valid ids in the error) for unknown ids; el.commands lists ids with label, shortcut and enabled state.
A nitro-command event (cancelable) fires for every command, host-added or built in, with { id, format }. preventDefault() lets a host replace built-ins such as file.save or file.open.
Readonly disables editing commands, including host ones flagged editing: true; tests cover hide, add, execCommand, cancel and readonly in all three apps.
README host-API section documents the option, the generated command-id list and an example; bundle-budget and all required checks green.

proposals.headline: Sort and Filter a spreadsheet, with AutoFilter arrows on the header row
proposals.today_caption: Today: there is no Data tab and no Sort or Filter command; the first row has no AutoFilter arrows, so you can't hide or sort rows from the UI.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: Data > Sort & Filter (Sort A to Z, Sort Z to A, Filter). AutoFilter arrows sit on the first row; the open menu searches, sorts and checks values, as in Excel.
proposals.why: Sorting a column and filtering a table are among the first things people do in a real spreadsheet, and Excel, Google Sheets, OnlyOffice and Collabora all put AutoFilter arrows on the header row. Nitro already keeps an autoFilter that arrives in a file and has SUBTOTAL / filtered-row helpers in the formula engine, but you can't turn Filter on, pick values, or Sort A to Z from the UI, and there is no Data tab. Wiring that up makes Nitro usable for everyday list work, and gives the already-approved right-click menu real Sort and Filter commands to call.
proposals.effort_note: 3–4 days (toggle AutoFilter, value menu, sort of the current region, and a valid autoFilter part on save)
proposals.risk: Medium. The saved autoFilter must open in Excel without a repair prompt, and hidden rows must stay out of copy, fill and later sort. Sort rearranges values in the current region (header row stays put) and is one undo step; formulas that pointed at moved cells follow Excel's usual relative-reference behaviour. A table without a clear header row should still get arrows on the first row of the used range, as Excel does.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: the Data tab and filter menu load with the lazily loaded Excel ribbon chunk (a few KB). Filtering hides rows already in the sheet view; it does not rescan the workbook on open. Sort is a single edit of the current region.
dod: A Data tab (and Home > Editing if it fits in the existing group without adding a ribbon row) offers Sort A to Z, Sort Z to A and Filter; Ctrl+Shift+L toggles AutoFilter on the current region.

With Filter on, the first row of the region shows AutoFilter arrows; the menu has Search, Sort A to Z / Z to A, Select All, per-value checkboxes and Blanks; OK hides non-matching rows and is one undo step.

Sort A to Z / Z to A rearranges the data rows of the current region and leaves the header row in place; the result saves as a valid autoFilter / sorted sheet that Excel and LibreOffice reopen without repair.

Nitro already has the model and edit ops to add, reply, resolve and delete Word comments, but there is no Review tab, no margin balloon, and no host event. Shipping the UI (and a small host hook) lets reviewers work in the document and lets embedding apps show or create the same comments.

Anchors must follow the selected text when the paragraph is edited, and resolved comments stay in the file but render in a quiet state, as Word does. No live multiplayer is in scope.

dod: A Review tab offers New Comment, Delete, Resolve, Previous and Next; Ctrl+Alt+M adds a comment on the current selection (or the word at the caret).

proposals.headline: Headers, footers and page numbers, like Word

proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: Insert > Header & Footer (Header, Footer, Page Number). The page shows a header with the document title and Page 1 of 1, as in Word.
proposals.why: Almost every professional Word document has a header, a footer or a page number, and people look for them on the Insert tab in Word, Google Docs, OnlyOffice and Collabora. Nitro already reads, paints and can set header and footer stories (the edit helpers landed with the earlier header/footer work), and the approved Print proposal will need those fields to show up on the printed page. What's missing is the Insert UI and a way to type into the header or footer in the document itself.
proposals.effort_note: 1–2 days (Insert group and in-page edit surface on top of the existing header/footer renderer and set-text helpers)
proposals.risk: Low to medium. The saved header, footer and page-number fields must be valid so Word opens the file without a repair prompt, and they must use the document's section (margins, first-page header if the file already has one). Typing in the header must not move the body text. A page-number field has to update when pages are added, not stay as a fixed '1'.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: the Header & Footer group and the in-page editor load with the lazily loaded Word Insert chunk (a small addition). Headers and footers already paint on each page today when a file contains them; this does not add work on open for files without them.
dod: Insert > Header & Footer offers Header, Footer and Page Number (the Font and Paragraph groups stay at two rows; this is a new Insert group). Choosing Header or Footer (or double-clicking the top or bottom margin) edits that story in place, with a clear Header or Footer label, as in Word.

proposals.headline: Right-click menus with the everyday commands, like Office

proposals.why: Right-click is how most people reach Cut, Copy, Paste, Insert row and Format Cells in Word, Excel and PowerPoint, and Google Docs, OnlyOffice and Collabora all copy it. In Nitro a right-click does nothing, so users who don't know the ribbon layout get stuck. The editor already has a context-menu framework and a Shift+F10 shortcut entry; they just aren't wired to right-click or filled with per-app commands.
proposals.effort_note: 2–3 days (menu framework exists; per-app item lists and wiring)
proposals.risk: Low to medium. Every item must call the same command as its ribbon button, so behaviour can't drift. Right-click must first move the selection to the clicked cell, word or shape (unless it is inside the current selection), as Office does. Host apps that need the browser menu can turn it off.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: the menu code and item lists load with each app's lazy ribbon chunk (a few KB). Nothing runs until the user right-clicks.
dod: Right-click (and Shift+F10 / the Menu key) opens an Office-style menu at the pointer in all three apps; Esc, click-away and arrow keys work, and it is screen-reader accessible (role=menu).
Excel: Cut, Copy, Paste Options, Insert…, Delete…, Clear Contents, Sort, Filter, Format Cells…, Row Height…, Column Width…; on row/column headers: Insert, Delete, Hide, Unhide.

Word: Cut, Copy, Paste Options, Font…, Paragraph…, Link…, bullets and numbering; PowerPoint: Cut, Copy, Paste, Duplicate, Delete, Bring to Front / Send to Back on shapes, and New Slide / Duplicate / Delete on the thumbnail rail.
Right-click moves the selection to the target first; disabled items are greyed out; a contextmenu="browser" attribute (and React prop) keeps the browser's own menu for hosts that want it.
Playwright tests cover one item per app plus keyboard open; bundle-budget and all required checks green.

proposals.headline: Print or save as PDF (Ctrl+P) with a clean print preview
proposals.today_caption: Today: the File menu has Open, Save a copy and Close but no Print. Ctrl+P in the document does nothing (console: "unsupported edit op file.print"), and the browser's own Print captures the toolbar, ribbon and status bar around the page.
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: File > Print… (Ctrl+P) opens a print view with destination (Save as PDF or a printer), page range, paper size, orientation and scale, next to a clean preview of the page.
proposals.why: Printing and saving as PDF are among the most common things people do with an Office file, and Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Google Docs and OnlyOffice all have File > Print with a preview. In Nitro, Ctrl+P is already bound to a Print command that isn't implemented, so nothing happens, and printing from the browser menu includes the app's toolbar and ribbon. Rendering each page cleanly for print reuses the page painters Nitro already has.
proposals.effort_note: 3–4 days (Word and PowerPoint pages first; Excel print areas and page breaks next)
proposals.risk: Medium. Long documents must render page by page without exhausting memory (draw into the print frame lazily, cap resolution). Excel needs sensible page breaks and must honour the file's print area and fit-to-page settings. Read-only, so files can't be damaged.
proposals.perf: No first-load change: the print view is its own lazily loaded chunk (a few KB). Print renders pages on demand at print resolution, so it doesn't slow normal viewing.
dod: File > Print… and Ctrl+P (inside the viewer) open a print view in all three apps; the browser's own Ctrl+P is not triggered.

The preview and output contain only the document pages (no app chrome), one per sheet of paper, using the file's paper size, margins and orientation; options for page range, scale, and in Excel selection / gridlines / fit sheet on one page.

proposals.headline: Tell host apps when a document has unsaved changes (nitro-dirty event, el.dirty, React onDirtyChange)
proposals.today_caption: Today: a host app embeds <nitro-docx> and the user has typed, but the app has no signal and still says "Last saved 9:02 AM".
proposals.mock_caption: Mockup: the host header flips to "Unsaved changes" from a nitro-dirty event; the same signal drives React onDirtyChange and a before-close warning.
proposals.why: Apps that embed Nitro need to show "Unsaved changes", autosave, and warn before the tab closes, which every Office and Google editor does. Today the only unsaved-changes signal lives inside Nitro's own full ribbon; a host using the plain element or <NitroViewer> hears nothing until it calls save(), and onChange only fires on save. That tracker also works by re-saving the whole file 350 ms after each burst of typing, so an engine-side modified flag is both the missing API and a speed-up.
proposals.effort_note: 2–3 days
proposals.risk: Low. Additive API. The flag must return to clean when undo reaches the saved state, and after save() or opening a new file.
proposals.perf: Replaces the ribbon's save-and-hash check (a full save after every edit burst) with a counter from the engine's edit history: less CPU and memory churn on large files. Event wiring goes in the lazily loaded editor chunk; the first-load loader stays within budget.
dod: Editable <nitro-docx>, <nitro-xlsx> and <nitro-pptx> expose a read-only dirty property and fire nitro-dirty (detail.dirty) only when it changes; save() and loading a file reset it; undo back to the saved state makes it clean again.
React: onDirtyChange(dirty) prop and isDirty() on the ref, with TypeScript types and a README example for autosave and a before-close warning.
Nitro's own ribbon indicator uses the same signal (the save-and-hash probe is removed); the demo's leave warning still works.
Tests for all three formats (edit → dirty, undo → clean, save → clean) plus the consumer-smoke example; bundle-budget and all required checks green.
proposals.status_note: Partly shipped in v0.2.0 (tagged ee9789c, published 2026-11-22): el.dirty + nitro-change. React onDirtyChange is in draft PRs #597 and #621 (agy cut-down of #597, opened 2026-11-24), both waiting for review.
